While the proteins are human in origin, they were expressed in E. coli and Sf9 cells.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The study focuses on structural proteomics (HDX-MS and XL-MS) to compare the conformational states of RORγ when bound to different DNA response elements (cRORE vs vRORE), ligands (SR19547), and coactivators (SRC3).

base_candidates_ranked.reason: The XL-MS data used label-free quantitation (LFQ) based on peak areas from MS1 full-scan filtering in Skyline.

modifier_candidates_ranked.reason: Explicit use of DSSO (disuccinimidyl sulfoxide) crosslinker with MS2-MS3 fragmentation strategy for sulfoxide cleavage.
Extensive use of Hydrogen-Deuterium Exchange Mass Spectrometry to monitor conformational changes.

workflow: RORγ:RORE samples were crosslinked in HBST buffer using disuccinimidyl sulfoxide (DSSO, Cayman chemicals).
Crosslinks were identified using the XlinkX algorithm implemented on Proteome Discoverer
Doublet pairs of ions with the targeted mass difference for sulfoxide fragmentation (31.9721 Da) ... were selected for HCD fragmentation
Typical HDX-MS peptide identification was performed using a previously described automated liquid handling robot
differential: Pair-wise comparisons were made using ‘MSstats’ package implemented in the Skyline browser to calculate relative fold changes and significance
Significant changes were defined as log 2 fold change was less than -1 or greater than 1
search_parameters: Cysteine carbamamidylation and methionine oxidation were considered as a fixed and a dynamic modification, respectively.
Crosslinks were considered for lysine, threonine, serine, and tyrosine residues

Ontology_ProcessingAndDifferential_promp.notes: The dataset contains two distinct structural proteomics modalities: XL-MS (using DSSO) and HDX-MS. The XL-MS analysis specifically utilizes an MS2-MS3 approach to identify crosslinks via the characteristic sulfoxide cleavage of DSSO.
